scope: Proposition 10.15 (Fixed-code arm test) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 118-119. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let λ = log R. In the finite shifted address model, fix a code, let mj be its number of occupied boxes at level j, and let ej be the sum of its two monochrome ranks. Put T = X j mj, E = X j ej, 118 and let M be the number of terminal entries. For each ζ > 0, one can choose a fixed sufficiently large R and sufficiently small fixed deletion tolerances so that, as the minimum sampling radius tends to infinity, P{the code’s chord constraints are realizable} ≤ exp{−βλE + ζλT + CR,ζM}. (10.23) The statement is for codes with the regular-slot deletion bound of Lemma 10.8. It is uniform over such finite codes and over arbitrary exact chord endpoints inside their recorded boxes. Small fixed errors in sampling radii or inward integer rounding are absorbed by increasing the minimum permitted radius.
